analysis.title: Situation Room: 3Q26 IG fundamentals final update: more earnings, stable debt
key_insights: With 3Q results in for 89% of US IG issuers in BofA's sample (non-financial, non-utility), IG credit fundamentals improved in 3Q. Net leverage fell, led by BBBs, to the lowest since 2021 by the headline figure, and gross leverage hit the lowest since 2018.

Median gross leverage fell to 2.45x in 3Q. Median net leverage fell to 1.91x from 1.95x in 2Q in the text, while Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 6 give 1.89x. The report is internally inconsistent on this figure.

Median YoY LTM EBITDA growth accelerated to +9.9% in 3Q from +9.3% in 2Q, the highest since 2021. The Revenue and EBITDA section separately says median YoY EBITDA growth declined to 10.6% from 11.3%. The two figures use different definitions and conflict in direction as written.
Median YoY revenue growth was steady at +7.4% in 3Q versus +7.6% in 2Q, near the highest since 3Q22. Median LTM revenue growth was +1.8% QoQ versus +1.9%.
Interest coverage rose to 10.7x, the highest since 3Q23. Borrowing costs were roughly stable.
Debt growth stayed slow. Gross debt was +1.0% YoY (vs +0.8% in 2Q) and net debt +0.7% YoY (vs -0.5% in 2Q). Gross debt was mostly flat in 2023-2024 and has grown modestly in 2026.
By rating, 3Q gross leverage was 2.67x for BBBs and 1.87x for A-rated issuers. Net leverage was 2.12x for BBBs and 1.32x for A-rated issuers, versus 1.31x for A-rated in 2Q.
Aggregate net leverage ex. Mag 7 was 1.72x. For A-rated issuers aggregate net leverage fell to 1.35x from 1.42x. For BBBs aggregate net leverage fell to 2.03x.
Cash and securities rose +1.7% QoQ in 3Q, in line with the seasonal pattern, and +1.4% YoY versus +5.9% in 2Q. Cash was 6.1% of assets, and long-term debt was 91.6% of total debt.
Margins declined in 3Q. Median gross margin was 38.8% versus 40.2% in 2Q, and median EBITDA margin was 20.4%.
Median YoY capex growth slowed to +6.4% from +9.1%. LTM capex as a share of EBITDA fell to 19.9% from 20.2%, below the 2024 highs.
Net debt to enterprise value has stayed relatively stable since 2015 even though net leverage has trended up.
Daily supply: US IG issuance was $3.1bn across 3 deals on Nov 18, $31.3bn week to date and $148.6bn month to date. This week's new issues trade 3bps tighter on average from pricing.
Estimated IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds rose to $4.8bn on Nov 18 from $0.2bn on Nov 4. Dealer inventory DV01 was -$5.1mn versus -$7.1mn on Nov 4.
HG fund flows: daily inflow was $783mn on Nov 17 versus $356mn on Nov 16. Average daily flow was -$160mn in November versus +$708mn in October.

Foreign demand proxies: net dealer volume before 8am ET in 1-10yr bonds was -$139mn on Nov 18 versus -$153mn the day before. Dealer-to-affiliate volume 8am-noon ET was -$157mn for 1-10yr and -$49mn for 10yr+. Negative values denote net client buying.
earnings_insights: 3Q26 actual results are available for 89% of the 354 US IG non-financial non-utility issuers in BofA's sample. Figures are GAAP medians, using actuals where available and estimates otherwise.
Median YoY LTM EBITDA growth was +9.9% in 3Q (reported or estimated per the methodology) versus +9.3% in 2Q. Median YoY EBITDA growth was 10.6% versus 11.3% in 2Q, per the Revenue and EBITDA section.
Median YoY revenue growth was +7.4% in 3Q versus +7.6% in 2Q.
risk_factors: Net leverage for A-rated issuers rose at the median, to 1.32x from 1.31x, even as the aggregate fell.
Margins fell in 3Q, with gross margin at 38.8% versus 40.2% and EBITDA margin at 20.4%.
YoY growth in cash and securities slowed to +1.4% from +5.9%.
vol_and_positioning: Estimated IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds were $4.8bn on Nov 18, up from $0.2bn on Nov 4. Dealer inventory DV01 was -$5.1mn.
HG fund flows were +$783mn on Nov 17. Average daily HG flow was -$160mn in November versus +$708mn in October. Flows have been decoupled from 2-month returns since around Oct-2024.
